label: MikroTik hAP ax³ (C53UiG+5HPaxD2HPaxD)
description: MikroTik hAP ax³ - 4x 1G RJ45 plus 1x 2.5G RJ45 (eth1, which also carries passive PoE-in and PoE-out), dual-band 802.11ax (574 Mbit/s on 2.4 GHz, 1200 Mbit/s on 5 GHz).
notes: Vendor figures: 4x 1G Ethernet ports and 1x 2.5G Ethernet port that "supports PoE-in/out"; wireless 2.4 GHz 574 Mbit/s and 5 GHz 1200 Mbit/s (802.11ax). **The ax3 has five copper ports, not four**: the 2.5G port is ether1 (the manual's powering block reads "PoE-out Passive PoE Ether1, max out per port output (input < 30 V): 0.625 A" and "PoE-out total output power 15 W", and the same page lists "Number of 2.5G Ethernet ports 1 (supports PoE-in/out)"). An earlier copy of this box (`hap-ax3.json`) recorded four 1G ports, dropped the 2.5G port, put the PoE-out on eth4 and classed it `PoE+`; it also claimed the ax3 "trades a port for a faster CPU against the ax2" - it does not, it upgrades one of five. That file is absorbed here.

poe.note: PoE-out total output power 15 W for the single passive PoE-out port (ether1, 0.625 A ceiling at input < 30 V); the product table prints the same ceiling as "Total output current 0.625" and "Total output power 15" - 0.625 A x 24 V = 15 W. Product page: https://mikrotik.com/product/hap_ax3
